q: The novel 'Native Son' (1940), centred on the young Chicago man Bigger Thomas, was written by:
e: Native Son (1940), centred on the young Chicago man Bigger Thomas, was written by Richard Wright, a leading African-American author.

e: Their Eyes Were Watching God (1937), centred on Janie Crawford in Florida, was written by Zora Neale Hurston.

q: The historical novel 'Ben-Hur: A Tale of the Christ' (1880), centred on the Jewish prince Judah Ben-Hur, was written by:
e: Ben-Hur: A Tale of the Christ (1880), centred on the Jewish prince Judah Ben-Hur, was written by Lew Wallace.

e: The Scarlet Pimpernel (1905), about Sir Percy Blakeney rescuing French aristocrats during the Revolution, was written by Baroness Orczy.

e: Quo Vadis (1896), set in Rome in the time of Emperor Nero, was written by Polish author Henryk Sienkiewicz, later a Nobel laureate.

q: The poem 'The Rime of the Ancient Mariner' (1798), telling of a sailor cursed after killing an albatross, was written by:
e: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner (1798), about a sailor cursed after killing an albatross, was written by Samuel Taylor Coleridge.

q: The novel 'Vanity Fair' (1848), centred on the scheming Becky Sharp in Regency England, was written by:
e: Vanity Fair (1848), centred on the scheming Becky Sharp, was written by William Makepeace Thackeray.

q: The novel 'The Master and Margarita', written in the Soviet era and centred on a visit of the Devil to Moscow, was written by:
e: The Master and Margarita, about the Devil's visit to Moscow, was written by Soviet author Mikhail Bulgakov.

q: The Russian novel 'Oblomov' (1859), famous for its indolent landowner hero Ilya Oblomov, was written by:
e: Oblomov (1859), famous for its indolent landowner hero Ilya Oblomov, was written by Ivan Goncharov.

q: The novel 'Disgrace' (1999), centred on the disgraced professor David Lurie in post-apartheid South Africa, was written by:
e: Disgrace (1999), centred on disgraced professor David Lurie in post-apartheid South Africa, was written by J. M. Coetzee.

q: The Tamil novel 'One Part Woman', centred on the childless couple Kali and Ponna and the temple festival at Ardhanarishvara, was written by:
e: One Part Woman, centred on childless Kali and Ponna and the Ardhanarishvara temple festival, was written by Tamil author Perumal Murugan.

q: The Islington Commission (1912), officially the Royal Commission on the Public Services in India, was appointed to inquire into:

options.B: The working of the police in India
options.C: The condition of agriculture in India
options.D: The system of currency in India

e: The Islington Commission (1912), the Royal Commission on the Public Services in India, was appointed to inquire into the public services in India.

q: The Fowler Committee (1898) was appointed by the Government of India to examine and report on:

options.A: The famine relief administration in India
options.C: The development of railways in India

e: The Fowler Committee (1898) was appointed to examine and report on Indian currency, including the standard and exchange questions of the time.

q: The Sargent Committee (1944), whose report is known as the Sargent Plan, drew up a scheme for:

options.A: The reorganisation of the Indian Army
options.B: The expansion of technical education only in the provinces
options.D: The reform of the prison system in India

e: The Sargent Committee (1944), whose report is called the Sargent Plan, drew up a scheme for post-war educational development in India.

q: The Chagla Commission (1958), headed by Justice M. C. Chagla, was appointed to inquire into:

options.A: The working of the Life Insurance Corporation's branch offices
options.B: The procurement of stores for the Railways
options.C: The administration of the Employees' Provident Fund
options.D: The investments made by the Life Insurance Corporation in the Mundhra concerns

e: The Chagla Commission (1958), headed by Justice M. C. Chagla, inquired into the investments made by LIC in the Mundhra concerns.

q: The Report on Public Administration (1951), an early landmark study of administrative reform in independent India, was submitted by:
e: The Report on Public Administration (1951), an early landmark study of administrative reform in independent India, was submitted by A. D. Gorwala.

q: The Tyagi Committee (1958-59), officially the Direct Taxes Administration Enquiry Committee, was appointed to examine and report on:

options.A: The administration of indirect taxes in India
options.B: The administration of direct taxes in India
options.C: The working of the Reserve Bank of India
options.D: The audit of public sector undertakings

e: The Tyagi Committee (1958-59), the Direct Taxes Administration Enquiry Committee, examined the administration of direct taxes in India.

q: The Railway Corruption Enquiry Committee (1953-55), set up to inquire into corruption in the Railways, was chaired by:
e: The Railway Corruption Enquiry Committee (1953-55), set up to inquire into corruption in the Railways, was chaired by Acharya J. B. Kripalani.

options.C: The reorganisation of the Intelligence Bureau
options.D: India's military operations in the Sino-Indian war of 1962

e: The Henderson Brooks-Bhagat Committee was appointed after the 1962 war to inquire into India's military operations in the Sino-Indian war.

q: The Kapur Commission (1966), headed by Justice J. L. Kapur, was appointed to inquire further into:

options.A: The conspiracy behind the assassination of Mahatma Gandhi
options.B: The circumstances of the death of Lal Bahadur Shastri
options.C: The working of the Central Bureau of Investigation
options.D: The administration of the Delhi Police

e: The Kapur Commission (1966), headed by Justice J. L. Kapur, inquired further into the conspiracy behind the assassination of Mahatma Gandhi.

q: The Hota Committee (2004), headed by former UPSC Chairman P. C. Hota, is associated with recommendations on:
e: The Hota Committee (2004), headed by former UPSC Chairman P. C. Hota, made recommendations on civil services reforms.

options.B: The revolt of 1857 in the North-Western Provinces

e: The commission set up in 2022 on Scheduled Caste status for Dalit converts to other religions was chaired by Justice K. G. Balakrishnan, former Chief Justice of India.

q: 'Pedology' is the branch of science that deals with the study of:
e: Pedology is the branch of science dealing with the study of soil, including its origin, classification and distribution.

q: 'Epigraphy' is the branch of study that deals with:

options.B: Inscriptions on stones, coins and other materials

e: Epigraphy is the study of inscriptions on stones, coins and other materials, used as a source for history.

q: 'Etymology' is the branch of study that deals with:

options.B: The structure of the Earth's crust
options.C: The origin and historical development of words

e: Etymology deals with the origin and historical development of words and how their meanings have changed over time.

q: 'Bryology' is the branch of botany that deals with the study of:
e: Bryology is the branch of botany dealing with mosses and liverworts, the bryophytes.

q: The currency of South Africa is the:
e: The currency of South Africa is the rand, issued by the South African Reserve Bank.

q: The currency of Sweden is the:
e: The currency of Sweden is the krona, distinct from similarly named crowns of some neighbouring countries.

q: The currency of Canada is the:
e: The currency of Canada is the Canadian dollar, issued by the Bank of Canada.

q: The legislative capital of Sri Lanka is:
e: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte is the legislative capital of Sri Lanka, where its Parliament is located, while Colombo remains the executive and judicial capital.

q: The highest mountain peak of Antarctica is:
e: Mount Vinson is the highest mountain peak of Antarctica, rising in the Sentinel Range of the Ellsworth Mountains.

q: The tallest building in the world is the:
e: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai is the tallest building in the world, taller than the Shanghai Tower, Merdeka 118 and the Abraj Al Bait Clock Tower.

q: World AIDS Day is observed every year on:
e: World AIDS Day is observed every year on 1 December to raise awareness of HIV and AIDS and to remember those lost to the disease.

q: International Mother Language Day, proclaimed by UNESCO, is observed every year on:
e: International Mother Language Day, proclaimed by UNESCO, is observed every year on 21 February to promote linguistic and cultural diversity.

q: Good Governance Day in India, marking the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, is observed every year on:
e: Good Governance Day in India, marking the birth anniversary of Atal Bihari Vajpayee, is observed every year on 25 December.

q: The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram), a UNESCO World Heritage monument, is located in the State of:
e: The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram, a UNESCO World Heritage monument of the Pallava period, is located in Tamil Nadu.

q: The Lotus Temple, the Bahai House of Worship famous for its lotus-shaped structure, is located at:
e: The Lotus Temple, the Bahai House of Worship shaped like a lotus, is located in New Delhi.

q: The Western Ghats mountain range is also known by the name:
e: The Western Ghats mountain range is also known as the Sahyadri, running along the western coast of India.

q: The currency of Australia is the:
e: The currency of Australia is the Australian dollar, which replaced the Australian pound in 1966.

q: The National Academy of Indian Railways (NAIR) at Vadodara was earlier known by the name:
e: The National Academy of Indian Railways at Vadodara was earlier known as the Railway Staff College, the apex training institution for railway officers.

q: The corporate headquarters of the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL) is located at:
e: The corporate headquarters of DFCCIL, which builds and operates the Dedicated Freight Corridors, is located in New Delhi.

q: The corporate headquarters of the Konkan Railway Corporation Limited (KRCL) is located at:
e: The corporate headquarters of Konkan Railway Corporation Limited is located at Navi Mumbai, in CBD Belapur.

q: The Centre for Railway Information Systems (CRIS), the information technology organisation of Indian Railways, was set up in the year:
e: CRIS, the information technology organisation of Indian Railways, was set up in 1986 to develop and manage railway IT systems.

q: The Raising Day of the Railway Protection Force (RPF) is celebrated every year on:
e: The Raising Day of the Railway Protection Force is celebrated every year on 20 September, the day the RPF Act came into force in 1985.

e: SRESTHA, set up in 2016 for long-term strategic railway research, functions as a directorate under RDSO, the research organisation at Lucknow.

q: The Commission of Railway Safety organisation is headed by the officer designated as the:
e: The Commission of Railway Safety organisation is headed by the Chief Commissioner of Railway Safety, under the Ministry of Civil Aviation.

q: The Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Limited (MRVC) was incorporated in the year:
e: Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Limited, which executes Mumbai suburban railway projects, was incorporated in 1999.

e: The Zonal Railway Training Institute at Sini in Jharkhand functions under South Eastern Railway, headquartered at Garden Reach, Kolkata.

e: IRCTC Rail Connect is the official mobile application of IRCTC for booking reserved rail tickets, while UTS on Mobile is for unreserved tickets.

e: The Jamalpur Workshop of Eastern Railway, regarded as the first full-fledged railway workshop in India, was established in 1862.

e: Inter-Railway sports championships of Indian Railways are organised under the aegis of the Railway Sports Promotion Board.

e: DFCCIL, the special purpose vehicle for the Dedicated Freight Corridors, was incorporated in 2006 under the Ministry of Railways.

e: The Electric Loco Shed at Bondamunda of South Eastern Railway is located in Odisha, near Rourkela.

e: The Electric Loco Shed at Tatanagar is located in Jharkhand, Tatanagar being the railway station of Jamshedpur.

e: The Diesel Loco Shed at Gooty of South Central Railway is located in Andhra Pradesh, in Anantapur district.

e: The Electric Loco Shed at Barauni of East Central Railway is located in Bihar, in Begusarai district.

q: The Electric Loco Shed at New Katni Junction, which homes electric locomotives of the West Central Railway, is located in the State of:
e: The Electric Loco Shed at New Katni Junction of West Central Railway is located in Madhya Pradesh, in Katni district.

e: The Electric Loco Shed at Valsad of Western Railway is located in Gujarat, at the southern end of the state near Maharashtra.

e: The Nabinagar thermal power project of Bharatiya Rail Bijlee Company Limited, which supplies power to the Railways, is located in Aurangabad district of Bihar.

q: In Indian Railways, the designation 'AGM', borne by the second-in-command at a zonal railway headquarters, stands for:
e: AGM stands for Additional General Manager, the second-in-command at a zonal railway headquarters who assists the General Manager.

e: SDGM stands for Senior Deputy General Manager, the senior officer at zonal headquarters who also heads the vigilance organisation.

e: CHOD stands for Coordinating Head of Department, the head of a department at zonal headquarters who coordinates the work of that department.

e: DPO stands for Divisional Personnel Officer, the officer of the personnel branch at divisional level dealing with staff matters.

e: ASC stands for Assistant Security Commissioner, the Railway Protection Force officer assisting the Divisional Security Commissioner in a division.

e: ECRC stands for Enquiry-cum-Reservation Clerk, the commercial staff who attend to reservation and enquiry work at booking offices.

e: Sr. DCM stands for Senior Divisional Commercial Manager, the head of the commercial branch at divisional level.

e: The first stretch of Bengaluru Metro, opened in October 2011, ran between Baiyappanahalli and M. G. Road.

e: The Vivek Express series was introduced in 2011 to commemorate the 150th birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda.

e: The first section of Delhi Metro, opened in December 2002, was built between Shahdara and Tis Hazari on the Red Line.

e: The Chenab Rail Bridge of the USBRL project, the world's highest railway arch bridge, has been constructed by Afcons Infrastructure Limited.

e: The first Mahamana Express, flagged off in January 2016, ran between Varanasi and New Delhi.

e: Ente Katha or My Story, the frank autobiographical account first published in Malayalam, was written by Kamala Das.

e: Jhootha Sach, the two-part Hindi novel on the Partition of India and its aftermath, was written by Yashpal.

e: Chitralekha (1934), debating sin and virtue through the courtesan Chitralekha and the ascetic Kumaragiri, was written by Bhagwati Charan Verma.

e: Shekhar: Ek Jivani, the celebrated psychological Hindi novel left unfinished in two parts, was written by Agyeya.

e: Nirmala, centred on a young bride married to a much older widower, was written by Munshi Premchand.

e: Persuasion, published posthumously in 1817 and centred on Anne Elliot and Captain Wentworth, was written by Jane Austen.

e: Of Mice and Men (1937), centred on migrant ranch workers George Milton and Lennie Small, was written by John Steinbeck.

e: Love in the Time of Cholera (1985), centred on Florentino Ariza's lifelong wait for Fermina Daza, was written by Gabriel Garcia Marquez.
